rs.one_line: Cheap at about 9 to 10 times earnings because investors fear AI tools will cap Adobe's pricing and growth. Reported results are still solid, but no hard proof of lost customers either way.

why_fell.reason: Fear that AI image and design tools make Creative Cloud less needed, and software-wide sell-off
why_fell.evidence: Shares were down about 23% for 2026 by mid-March. A broad rout on AI-agent fears erased nearly $1 trillion across software. Bloomberg Intelligence noted Adobe's financials had changed little while the stock fell almost 40%.

why_fell.reason: CEO Shantanu Narayen announced he would step down after 18 years
why_fell.evidence: Stock fell more than 7% on the news. Analysts said the leadership uncertainty overshadowed a quarter that beat on sales.

why_fell.reason: Wave of analyst downgrades over AI pricing power and weak AI monetization
why_fell.evidence: William Blair cut to Market Perform citing intense competition and unclear pricing power, while calling shares inexpensive at about 9 times free cash flow. Barclays and Argus also cut.

why_fell.reason: Wells Fargo cut to Underweight on Oct. 12 after a survey and slower new recurring revenue
why_fell.evidence: Wells Fargo estimated organic net new recurring revenue fell over 40% in Q3 and must nearly double in Q4 to hit targets. Target cut to $225. Stock fell about 4% to roughly $232.

for_unfair.point: Latest quarter (ended Aug. 28) was a record: revenue $6.76 billion, up 12 to 13%; annual recurring revenue $27.5 billion; operating cash flow $2.52 billion. Full-year revenue and profit targets were raised.
AI-first recurring revenue grew about 150% from a year earlier and Adobe passed 1 billion monthly active users. Starting base is small, so this is not yet big.
Valuation is low: about 9.4 times forward earnings against a five-year average near 23. Targets of $200 to $267 still sit near the current price, so much bad news looks priced in.

for_fair.point: Downgrade wave is broad and recent: Wells Fargo and HSBC cut in October, Citi at Sell with $207 target on Nov. 4, Goldman at Sell with $200. Citi warned fiscal 2027 growth estimates may be too high.

Growth is expected to slow from about 12% this year to about 8% by fiscal 2028. William Blair says Firefly adoption looks tepid and it is unclear Adobe can charge for AI without cannibalizing subscriptions.

Rivals are pushing in: Canva reached $4 billion recurring revenue and launched AI 2.0 aimed at Adobe; Figma bought Weavy for AI image and video. Adobe is matching by adding OpenAI and Google models to Firefly.

rs.what_market_fears: That free or cheap AI tools from OpenAI, Google, Canva and Figma cap what Adobe can charge and slow new subscriptions. A new CEO adds execution risk during that shift.
rs.what_would_prove_it_wrong: Two quarters of sales growth below 8%, falling subscriber counts or price cuts, or AI-first revenue staying tiny while core Creative Cloud slows. Continued 12%+ growth with the new CEO would show the fear is overdone.
rs.next_date_to_watch: Mid-December 2026: fourth-quarter and fiscal 2027 outlook (exact date not confirmed). New CEO Anil Chakravarthy starts Dec. 1.

flag.note: Latest reported growth is 12 to 13%, well above the 8% line. Guidance for Q4 of $6.80 to $6.85 billion implies growth stays near that pace. Analysts warn of slowing, but not yet below 8%.

rs.not_found: No hard data on customers or pricing moving from Adobe to Canva, Figma, OpenAI or Google; only competitor commentary. Could not fetch Adobe's press release, Morningstar or S&P pages (blocked); Q3 figures come from Constellation Research and TIKR, not the filing. Wells Fargo's prior rating differs by source. Fiscal 2027 guidance not out yet.

companies.why: Ad revenue grew 26%, with gains it attributes to its AI ranking.

companies.basis: 10 to 15 times operating cash after stock pay. This measure ignores building spend, on the view that a bust lets these companies cut it.

rs.one_line: Ads are growing 26%, but spending of $135-145B this year has erased free cash and legal bills are piling up. The fall is partly deserved.

why_fell.reason: Spending is huge and rising
why_fell.evidence: 2026 capital spending guided to $135-145B. Q3 spending was $34.9B and free cash flow was negative $2.1B. Long-term debt rose to $80.9B from $58.7B at end of 2025. No 2027 figure given.

why_fell.reason: Stock dropped about 7% after Q3 report
why_fell.evidence: Shares fell as much as 7.6% on Oct 22 despite revenue beating estimates. Operating margin halved to 20%, mostly from a $9.9B legal charge. New non-voting share class also announced.

why_fell.reason: Legal bills and youth-safety trials
why_fell.evidence: $9.89B charge for an August deal with 52 state attorneys general, payments up to about $18.6B. A New Mexico judge ordered $25B on Oct 21; Meta will appeal. More youth trials are coming.

why_fell.reason: Debt kept off Meta's books
why_fell.evidence: Meta put its Hyperion campus into a joint venture (Blue Owl 80%, Meta 20%, about $27B of bonds) and is pitching a similar $12B+ El Paso deal with BlackRock. Meta leases the sites back and books rent, not capital spending.

for_unfair.point: Core ad business is accelerating. Q3 revenue up 26% to $64.6B; ad impressions up 10% and price per ad up 14%. Q4 revenue guided to $73-76B.
Without the one-time legal charge, Q3 operating income was $22.9B and EPS $7.40, well above the $5.46 analysts expected. Meta expects strong revenue growth through 2027.
Valuation is low for its growth: about 18-20x expected earnings versus 29x at the February 2025 peak. Analysts are almost all Buy. Reported by secondary sites; price targets vary.

for_fair.point: Free cash flow turned negative in Q3 (minus $2.1B versus plus $10.6B a year earlier). Nine-month free cash flow was $11.0B. Spending is 43% of sales.
Legal risk is real and open-ended: a $25B New Mexico judgment (appeal pending), youth trials, and an FTC appeal of its 2025 antitrust win. Experts say the $25B may be cut on appeal.
Off-balance-sheet leases hide commitments. Chips lose value in a few years while leases may run shorter than the campuses. Hyperion is growing to 5 gigawatts, near $50B.

rs.what_market_fears: That AI building spending keeps climbing while returns stay unproven, leaving no free cash, more debt and leases, and growing court bills. Not a fear of falling ad sales.
rs.what_would_prove_it_wrong: Ad growth falling below 10% while spending stays above 35% of sales. Also a 2027 spending plan far above 2026 with no matching revenue, or the New Mexico penalty standing in full.
rs.next_date_to_watch: Q4 2026 earnings, expected late January 2027 (per one secondary source, unconfirmed). Should include the first 2027 spending plan. Class C share dividend effective Jan 19, 2027.

flag.note: Ad revenue grew 26% in Q3, far above the 10% line. Spending is 43% of sales, so only half the flag condition is met.

rs.not_found: No 2027 capital spending figure; Meta has not given one (Q2 call said only that it is keeping flexibility). Could not confirm 2026 EU regulator actions or the FTC appeal's current stage (appeal filed Jan 2026, Boasberg ruled for Meta Nov 2025). Meta's balance-sheet lease totals not found. Current share price not independently confirmed. Sources conflicted on earlier capex ranges; the October range comes from the Meta release.

rs.one_line: Fell on AI-slowdown fear, a bearish call and wind losses, not on lost orders; orders and backlog are strong, but cash flow leans on customer deposits.

why_fell.reason: AI-slowdown fear
why_fell.evidence: Shares fell 8.6% on 14 Sep 2026 after an essay by Anthropic's CEO urged slowing frontier AI. Eaton and Vertiv fell about 7.6%. Sentiment, not a lost order.

why_fell.reason: Bearish analyst call
why_fell.evidence: Same day, a new Sell rating said shares could fall about 50%, and that 2027 turbines were ordered at lower prices. Reported by secondary sites only; no primary report seen.

why_fell.reason: Wind outlook got worse
why_fell.evidence: On 28 Oct 2026 shares fell as much as 6.6% though results beat. 2026 wind loss now $400-500M, up from about $400M. Stock closed near -1% by afternoon.

why_fell.reason: Sector selloff in AI-power stocks
why_fell.evidence: Stock fell about 6% as AI power names gave back a Monday rally. Exact date not confirmed; likely November.

for_unfair.point: Q3 orders $29.3B (up 96%), backlog $197B. Gas backlog rose 53 to 64 GW as 13 GW of slot reservations converted to orders. Management signed slots into 2032.
Asked directly about financing trouble, exits from slot reservations or slower conversion, the CEO said no. Terms for securing equipment are unchanged. About 80% of customers are non-data-center.
Power margin 21.4% and Electrification 19.1%. Company raised 2026 free cash flow guide to $16-17B and doubled buyback to $20B.

for_fair.point: Of $5.4B Q3 free cash flow, $5.3B was working capital, mainly customer down payments and slot reservations. That cash is borrowed from customers and reverses as turbines ship.
Wind still loses money (2026 loss $400-500M; Q3 margin 2.6%). Management said Q4 gas order price per kW will be lower than Q3.

2001-02 precedent: GE turbine orders and shipments were forecast to fall 80% or more in two years; customers rescheduled deliveries and Calpine cancelled 34 GE turbines. Top 20 customers were 70% of demand.

rs.what_market_fears: That AI data-center spending slows, customers walk from slot reservations, and a record order boom turns into a 2001-style bust. Also that deposit-fed cash flow is peak.
rs.what_would_prove_it_wrong: Slot reservations converting to firm orders on schedule, gas backlog above 70 GW, no reported cancellations, and free cash flow staying strong after deposits stop growing.
rs.next_date_to_watch: Q4 and full-year 2026 results, late January 2026-27 (about 28 Jan 2027, date not confirmed); watch slot reservation balance (58 GW) and conversions.

flag.note: No cancellations found. Slot reservations fell 63 to 58 GW because 13 GW converted to orders; CEO said no exit requests. Data-center share only about 20%.

facts.item: Trailing free cash flow and deposit share
facts.value: About $17.1B trailing 12 months (my sum: 9 months 2026 $15.3B + Q4 2025 $1.8B). Q3 alone $5.4B, with $5.3B from working capital, mainly down payments and slot reservations. Total contract liabilities not found.
facts.source: Q3 2026 8-K; Q3 call transcript; Q4 2025 results

facts.item: Latest quarter orders, backlog, gas GW
facts.value: Orders $29.3B (up 96%). Backlog $197B (equipment $104B, services $93B). Gas: firm backlog 64 GW (from 53), slot reservations 58 GW (from 63), total 122 GW; target 130+ GW by year end.
About 20% of gas customers are data centers, about 80% traditional (about 100 customers, 25 countries). Share of GW not given. Electrification data-center orders over $6B year to date.
Revenue $52B, adjusted EBITDA margin 20%, free cash flow at least $22B cumulative 2025-28, Power margin 22%. Set 9 Dec 2025. Not seen restated in Q3 2026 release.
facts.source: GE Vernova press release / Business Wire

facts.value: Cash about $16.8B (about $17B), up $4B in the quarter. Total debt not found, so net cash not confirmed. Plans about $4.5B new debt for $9B Trench deal; stays under 1x debt to EBITDA.

facts.item: GE gas turbine orders after 2001-02 bust
facts.value: GE Power cut about 2,500 jobs (July 2002). US orders and shipments forecast down 80% or more over two years. Albany plant: 120 turbines in 2003 vs 244 prior year. Calpine cancelled 34 GE gas turbines. Exact GE order counts not found.
facts.source: Power Engineering / OGJ / GE press release

facts.value: 14 Sep: -8.6% on AI-slowdown essay plus Sell initiation. 28 Oct: down as much as 6.6% on a worse wind loss outlook despite a beat. Later AI-power sector selloff (date unconfirmed).
